theme: The trip that slows people down

linkedin.text:
Most incentive itineraries are too full. The instinct is understandable — you are spending real money, so you fill the days. The result is a group that comes home tired and remembers a blur.

This is the Philippines, from a programme we produced with deliberate space in it. Two anchored days, one long boat afternoon, and evenings that were allowed to run without a schedule.

The argument is not softness. It is retention. People form the connections you are paying for in the unstructured hours — the boat ride, the walk back, the second drink — not during the team activity you booked to create them.

Getting this right is harder than it sounds. An empty afternoon has to feel like generosity, not neglect. That means options quietly available, staff who know where everyone is, and one genuinely excellent thing anchoring each day so nobody feels the trip is thin.

Want a programme with room to breathe in it? Tell us what your team is carrying this year.
